claims.text: The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr alloy has a random chemical distribution.
Annealing HfNbTaTiZr at 800°C induces short-range chemical order.
Increasing the annealing duration progressively increases short-range chemical order.
The degree of short-range chemical order can be quantified using atom-probe tomography or high-resolution diffraction.
Increased short-range chemical order increases local bond stiffness.
Increased short-range chemical order alters the local potential-energy landscape.
The changes in local bond stiffness and potential-energy landscape reduce dislocation mobility.
Increased short-range chemical order modifies lattice anharmonicity.
Reduced dislocation mobility caused by short-range chemical order improves elevated-temperature yield-strength retention.
Annealed samples with enhanced short-range chemical order will have higher elastic stiffness than the as-cast baseline.
Annealed samples with enhanced short-range chemical order will retain higher yield strength at elevated temperatures than the as-cast baseline.
Annealed samples with enhanced short-range chemical order will have a lower thermal-expansion coefficient than the as-cast baseline.
The predicted effects should hold from room temperature to approximately 1000 K under quasi-static strain rates.
The predicted effects are limited to samples in which the annealing protocol induces a moderate degree of short-range chemical order.
